at the kings standing before her. At that moment she saw Kåñëa. Then, while His enemies looked
on, the Lord seized the princess, who was eager to mount His chariot."***

  These verses mean: "She shyly waited for the arrival of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.
She looked at the kings standing before her. Then, with an agitated heart, she saw the infallible
Supreme Lord." These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 376-378


    An example in sambhoga of gazing and conversation in relation to the unmarried girls of Vraja
is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.52.55):


täsäà väsäàsy upädäya
   népam äruhya satvaraù
hasadbhiù prahasan bälaiù
   parihäsam uväca ha


  "Taking the girls' garments, He (Kåñëa) quickly climbed to the top of the kadamba tree. Then, as
He laughed loudly and His companions also laughed, He addressed the girts jokingly."***

   Here it may be said that although the gopés already had very exalted love for Lord Kåñëa, Lord
Kåñëa still manifested this joking pastime to openly display that love and to enjoy a certain kind of
loving pastime with them. Scholars learned in rasa-çästra yearn to relish this display of the gopés'
love. In this pastime Lord Kåñëa does not touch the gopés or enjoy other kinds of sambhoga pastimes
with them. This kind of pürva-rasa is called "lajjä-ccheda" (breaking the shyness). It is one of the
different kinds of sambhoga. These different kinds of sambhoga are described in these words of

Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa, Text 66:


nayana-prétiù prathamaà
   cintä-saìgas tato 'tha saìkalpaù
nidrä-cchedas tanutä
   viñaya-nivåttis trapä-näçaù
unmädo mürchä måtir
   ity etäù smara-daçä daçaiva syuù


   "Some other authorities list the stage of sambhoga in this way: 1. nayana-préti (falling in love by
seeing the beloved), 2. cintä (thinking of the beloved), 3. saìkalpa (deciding to pursue the beloved),
4. nidrä-ccheda (loss of sleep), 5. tanutä (becoming emaciated), viñaya-nivåtti (becoming oblivious
to everything except the beloved), 7. trapä-näça (destroying shyness), 8. unmäda (becoming wild), 9.
mürchä (fainting), and 10. måti (death)."

   This condition of breaking shyness is the most exalted state in anuräga. Even when they accept
death, the last of these ten states, the gopés do not abandon their shyness. To relish this kind of
anuräga (breaking the gopés' shyness), Lord Kåñëa arranged these joking pastimes. In these pastimes
Lord Kåñëa said to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.11):


na mayodita-pürvaà vä
   anrtam tad ime viduù


   "I have never before spoken a lie, and these boys know it. Therefore, O slender-waisted girls,
please come forward, either one by one or all together, and pick out your clothes."***

   That the gopés' love for Lord Kåñëa is never broken and remained unchanged in every situation
(even when Lord Kåñëa laughed at them) is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (01.229):


hasadbhiù. . .


   "Lord Kåñëa laughed loudly and His companions also laughed,"

  Here the word "bäla" indicated Lord Kåñëa's friends. Only persons who are Lord Kåñëa's friends
may touch His body. Other's cannot. Lord Kåñëa friends are described in these words of Gautaméya
Tantra, Prathamävaraëa-püjä:


däma-sudäma-vasudäma-
  kiìkiëér gandha-puñpakaiù

antaùkaraëa-rüpäs te
   kåñëasya parikértitäù
ätmäbhedena te püjyä
   yathä kåñëas tathaiva te


   "With fragrant flowers Dämä, Sudämä, Vasudämä, and Kiìkiëé worshiped Lord Kåñëa. These
boys were all praised by Lord Kåñëa Himself. These boys all know Lord Kåñëa's heart. Their hearts
are not different from Lord Kåñëa's heart. As Lord Kåñëa is worthy of worship, so are they."

   Because these pastimes of Lord Kåñëa's relishing the gopés' anuräga love for Him are confidential,
Lord Kåñëa pretended these activities were all a joke. This joking pretense is not incompatible with
these pastimes. On the contrary, Lord Kåñëa joking enhances the bliss of the pastimes. The great
sage Sukadeva Gosvami describes Lord Kåñëa's purpose in performing these activities. The sage
explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.18):


bhagavän ähatä vékñya
   çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù
skandhe nidhäya väsäàsi
   prétaù proväca sa-smitam


   "When the Supreme Lord saw how the gopés were struck with embarrassment, He was satisfied
by their pure loving affection. Putting their clothes on His shoulder, the Lord smiled and spoke to
them with affection."***

   In this verse the word "ähatäù" means {.sy 168}approached". Or, "ähaöaù" may also mean {.sy
168}Although they had renounced almost all shyness, because of their feminine nature a small
fragment of shyness remained. Because of this remaining shyness they gently bent their bodies."
The word "çuddha-bhäva-prasäditaù" means "pleased at heart by relishing the gopés' splendid love,
love that showed their longing to be with Him and their being enchanted by Him".
   The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19):


yüyaà vivasträ yad apo dhåta-vratäù. . .


   "(Lord Kåñëa said:) You girls bathed naked while executing your vow, and that is certainly an
offense against the demigods. To counteract Your sin you should offer obeisances while placing
your joined palms above your heads. Then you should take back your lower garments."***

   In order to see the last remnants of the gopés' shyness come to their final end Lord Kåñëa spoke
these joking words. The next verse explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.20):

ity acyutena. . .


   "Thus the young girls of Våndävana, considering what Lord Acyuta had told them, accepted that
they had suffered a falldown from their vow by bathing naked in the river. But they still desired to
successfully complete their vow, and since Lord Kåñëa is Himself the ultimate result of all pious
activities, they offered their obeisances to Him to cleanse away all their sins."***

   In this way Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the king of sages, reveals first the gopés'being enchanted by
Lord Kåñëa and their longing to associatte with Him, and then their obedience to His command. In
the next verse Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé explains (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.22):


dåòhaà pralabdhäs trapayä ca häpitäù
   prastobhitäù kréòana-vac ca käritah
vasträëi caiväpahåtäny athäpy amum-
   tä näbhyasüyan priya-saìga-nirvrtäh


   "Although the gopés had been thoroughly cheated, deprived of their modesty, ridiculed and made
to act just like toy dolls, ana although their clothing had been stolen, they did not feel at all
inimical toward Sré Kåñëa. Hather, they were simply joyful to have this opportunity to associate
with their beloved."***

   In the verse the word "dåòham" means {.sy 168}greatly", and "pralabdhäù" means "cheated". The
cheating of the gopés is described here in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.19. "Trapayä häpitäù" means
"deprived of their modesty". This is descibed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. "Prastobhitäù' here
means "mocked". Lord Kåñëa mocked the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.22.10. Lord Kåñëa's
making the gopés act like toy dolls is desscribed in His making them stand with folded palms on the
pretext of performing atonement. Even though Lord Kåñëa cheated them and teased them in many
ways, the gopés did not find fault with Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary. It is said here that even though
He had stolen their garments, the gopés did not feel eneimical toward Lord Kåñëa. On the contrary.
They were plunged into bliss because they had an opportunity to associate with their beloved.
These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 379-382


   Because they were brähmaëés, the yajïa-patnés were not qualified to associate with with Lord
Kåñëa as the gopés did. Still, the yajïa-patnés did have an ecstatic sentiment that was something like
pürva-räga. Gazing at Lord Kåñëa and conversing with Him, they experienced something in some
ways like sambhoga. They experienced sambhogäbhäsa (the reflection of sambhoga). After the
winter season had ended and summer had come, Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with the yajna-patnés
became visible. The beginning of these pastimes is desacribed in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam

(10.22.29):

atha gopaiù parivåto
   bhagavän devaké-sutaù
vrndävanäd gato düraà
   cärayan gäù sahägrajah


   "Some time later Lord Kåñëa, the son of Devaké, surrounded by His cowherd friends and
accompanied by His elder brother, Balaräma, went a good distance away from Våndävana, herding
the cows."***

   This verse means: "After Lord Kåñëa had given His mercy to the unmarried girls of Vraja, a
summer day came". That the day was a summer day distinguishes this pastime from the previous
pastime (which occurred in the winter). On this day Lord Kåñëa was accompanied by Lord
Balaräma. That is indicated here by the word "sägrajaù" (with His elder brother). Here the phrase "a
good distance away from Våndävana" indicates that Kåñëa and the boys were in the hilly part of
Kämyavana. That they were in the hills is seen by the fact that they decorated their bodies with
mineral pigments from the hills. That place is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.22.36):


tarüëäà namra-çäkhänäà
   madhyato yamunäà gatah


   "Thus moving among the trees, whose branches were bent low by their abundance of twigs,
fruits, flowers and leaves, Lord Kåñëa came to the Yamunä River."***

   With Vraja to their south and the Yamunä to the west, they entered a clearing to enjoy
pastimes. To the south was Mathurä City, and to the north was the place where some yäjïika-
brähmaëas lived. The home of these brahmana's was near King Kaàsa's palace. That is seen in
these words describing the thoughts of these brähmaëas (Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.23.52):


kaàsäd bhétä na cäcalan


   "Thus reflecting on the sin they had committed by neglecting Lord Kåñëa, they (the yäjïika-
brähmaëas) became very eager to see Him. But being afraid of King Kaàsa, they did not dare go to
Vraja."***

   In this way it is seen that those brähmaëas did not go to meet Lord Kåñëa. The summer qualities
of that day are described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.30):

nidäghärkätape tigme
   chäyäbhiù sväbhir ätmanaù
atapatrayitan vikñya
   drumän äha vrajaukasaù


   "When the sun's heat became intense, Lord Kåñëa saw that the trees were acting as umbrellas by
shading Him, and thus He spoke as follows to His boyfriends."***

   In this verse the phrase "nidäghärkätape tigme" is a locative absolute. The yajna-patnis'
sambhogäbhäsa (reflection of sambhoga) is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.21-23):


yamunopavane 'çoka-
   nava-pallava-mandite
vicarantaà våtaà gopaih
   sägrajaà dadåçuù striyaù


   "Along the river Yamunä, within a garden decorated with buds of açoka trees, they caught sight
of Him strolling along in the company of the cowherd boys and His elder brother, Balaräma.***


çyämaà hiraëya-paridhià vanamälya-barha-
   dhätu-praväla-naöa-veñam anuvratäàse
vinyasta-hastam itareëa dhunänam abjaà
   karëotpalälaka-kapola-mukhäbja-häsam


   "His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather, colored
minerals, sprigs of Mower buds, and a garland of forest flowers and leaves, He was dressed just like a
dramatic dancer. He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a
lotus. Lilies graced His ears, His hair hung down over His cheeks, and His lotuslike face was
smiling."***


präyaù-çruta-priyatamodaya-karëa-pürair
   yasmin nimagna-manasas tam athäkñi-randhraiù
antaù praveçya su-ciraà parirabhya täpaà
   präjïaà yathäbhimatayo vijahur narendra


   "O ruler of men, for a long time those brahmana ladies had heard about Kåñëa, their beloved,
and His glories had become the constant ornaments of their ears. Indeed, their minds were always
absorbed in Him. Through the apertures of their eyes they now forced Him to enter within their

hearts, and then they embraced Him within for a long time. In this way they fionally gave up the
pain of separation from Him, just as sagesa give up the anxiety of false ego by embracing their
innermost consciousness."***

   In this verse (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.23.23) the word {.sy 168}abhimatayaù" means: "false ego",
and the phrase {.sy 168}prajnam tapam vijahuù" means "as the sages, situated in spiritual trace,
become free of all sufferings, so these women also became free of all sufferings".

   One of those brähmaëés, becoming free of their previous disqualifications, attained in her heart
pürva-räga love for Lord Kåñëa and then enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him, pastimes that begin
with touching Him. This attainment of hers is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.35):


tatraikä vidhåtä bharträ
   bhagavantaà yathä-çrutam
hådopaguhya vijahau
   dehaà karmänubandhanam


   "One of ther ladies had been forcibly kept back by her husband. When she heard the others
describe the Supreme Lord Kåñëa, she embraced him within her heart and gave up her material
body, the basis of bondage to material activity."***

  When she gave up the brahmana body she had attained by past karma, then he disqualification
was destroyed and she was able to embrace Lord Kåñëa in her heart. In that way she attained Lord
Kåñëa's association. This is described in these words of Bhagavad-gétä (8.6):


yaà yaà väpi smana bhävam. . .


   "Whatever state of being one remembers when he quits this body, O son of Kunté, that state he
will attain without fail."*

   The statement that she attained Lord Kåñëa's association means that she attained the form of a
gopé. She did not attain the form of a brähmaëé and in that form associate with Lord Kåñëa. That
Lord Kåñëa's close associates were all cowherd people is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.23.37):


evaà lélä-nara-vapuù. . .


  "Thus the Supreme Lord, appearing like a human being to perform His pastimes, imitated the
ways of human society. He enjoyed pleasing His cows, cowherd boyfriends and cowherd girlfriends

with His beauty, words, and actions."***

   In this verse it is said that Lord Kåñëa enjoyed pleasing the cows and cowherd people. He did not
enjoy pastimes with others, at least not in the land of Vraja. In Vraja that yajïa-patné could not
enjoy pastimes with Lord Kåñëa without becoming a gopé. She thus entered the Vraja that is not
manifested in the material world. In that unmanifested Vraja Lord Kåñëa enjoys many different
pastimes, pastimes without limit. This is explained in the Kåñëa-sandarbha. Therefore there is
nothing wrong in her death. She yearned to attain Lord Kåñëa. With a great effort she struggled to
attain Him. In that way she attained a very exalted relationship (rasa) with Him. Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.23.35 quoted above was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

In the autumn after (Lord Çré Kåñëa's pastime of stealing the gopés' garments) all the vraja-gopés
enjoyed sambhoga pastime with Lord Kåñëa, pastimes born of the gopés' purva-raga love for Him,
pastimes that begin with gazing at Lord Kåñëa. These sambhoga pastimes are described (in the
scriptures). Although the unmarried girls of Vraja had already attained Lord Kåñëa's association,
theydid not feel fulfilled. Their purva-raga love for Him had still not attained its full nature. Still,
at least one gopés had enjoyed pastimes with Lord Kåñëa, as is seen in these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.21.17):


pürëäù pulindyaù. . .


   "The aborigine women of the Våndävana area become disturbed by lust when they see the grass
marked with reddish kuìkuma
powder. Endowed with the color of Kåñëa's lotus feet, this powder originally decorated the breasts
of His beloveds, and when the aborigine women smear it on their faces and breasts, they give up all
their anxiety."***

   Still, many other gopés had not yet even touched Lord Kåñëa. This is seen in these words spoken
by the gopés in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.29.36):


yarhy ambujäkña. . .


    "O lotus-eyed one, the goddess of fortune considers it a festive occasion whenever she touches
the soles of Your lotus feet. You are very dear to the residents of the forest, and therefore we will
also touch those lotus feet. From that time on we will be unable even to stand in the presence of
any other man, for we will have been fully satisfied by You."***

   When the gopés first heard Lord Kåñëa's flute-music they at first tried to supress the ecstatic

emotions that came to overwhelm them. From this it may be seen that they had not yet directly
enjoyed sambhoga pastimes with Him. Also, because they had not yet enjoyed sambhoga pastimes
with Him, Lord Kåñëa at first rejected them, and they then appealed to Him. These pastimes are
seen in Çrémad-Bhägavatam, Canto 10, Chapter 29, in the passage that begins with these words
(Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.29.4):


niçamya gétaà tad anaìga-vardhanaà
   vraja-striyaù kåñëa-gåhéta-mänasäù
äjagmur anyonyam alakñitodyamäù
   sa yatra känto java-lola-kundaläù


   "When the young women of Våndävana heard Kåñëa's flute song, which arouses romantic
feelings, their minds were captivated by the Lord. They went to where their lover waited, each
unknown to the others, moving so quickly that their earrings swung back and forth."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

Jealous anger (mäna) may bring separation (vipralambha) of Lord Kåñëa and His beloved. This is
seen in the following words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 93):


aher iva gatiù premëä
   sva-bhäva-kuöilä bhavet
ato hetor ahetoç ca
   yünor mäna udaïcati


   "The progress of loving affairs between young couples is by nature crooked, like the movement of
a snake. Becuase of this, two types of nager arise between young couples-anger with cause and anger
without cause."*

   Jealous anger without a cause is described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-
prakaraëa (Text 70):


ahetur neti nety ukter
   hetor yan mäna ucyate
asya praëaya eva syän
   mänasya padam uttamam

  "When without any cause the beloved says `No. No.' and rejects the lover, this is called jealous
anger (mäna). This is the highest state of loving jealous anger."

   Jealous anger is thus with a cause and without a ccause. Jealous anger with a cause is described in
these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 71):


hetur érñyä-vipakñäder
   viçiñöye preyasä kåte
bhävaù praëaya-mukhyo 'yam
   érñyä-mänatvam åcchati


   "When the lover gives special attention to a certain beloved, then all the rivals of the beloved
become jealous. In this way what was once love becomes jealous anger. This is anger with cause."

  Jealous anger is also described in these words of Ujjvala-nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa
(Text 72):


snehaà vinä bhayaà na syän
   nerñyä ca praëayaà vinä
tasmän mäna-prakäro 'yaà
   dvayoù prema-prakäçakaù


   "Without love there cannot be fear (for the loss of the beloved), and without love there cannot
be jealousy. For this reason fear and jealousy may be manifestations of love."

   Jealous anger is seen in the following words of Hari-vaàça, Viñëu-parva (66.4 and 65.50):


ruñitäm iva täà devéà
   snehät saìkalpayann iva
bhéta-bhéto 'ti-çanakair
   viveça yadu-nandanaù

rüpa-yauvana-sampannä
   sva-saubhägyena garvitä
abhimänavaté devé
   çrutvaiverñyä-vaçaà gatä


   "As He slowly entered the palace, Lord Kåñëa, who is feared by fear itself, and who is the
descendent of Maharaja Yadu, lovingly meditated on His angry queen Satyabhämä."

  "Meanwhile, hearing (how her rival Rukmiëé had attained a pärijäta flower from Indraloka),
Queen Satyabhämä, who was very proud of her opulent beauty and youthfulness, bexcame
overwhelmed with jealous anger."

   When the beloved suspects the lover no longer loves her, then jealous anger with cause is
manifest. Lord Kåñëa enjoys teasing His beloved in this way (to make her angry because she
suspects He no longer loves her). An example of such teasing is seen in these words Lord Kåñëa
spoke to Queen Rukmiëé (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.29):


tvad-vacaù çrotu-kämena
   kñvelyäcaritam aìgane


   "I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say."***

Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.30):


mukhaà ca prema-samrambha-
  sphuritädharam ékñitum. . .


   "I wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes
throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown."***

  Queen Rukmiëé refuted Lord Kåñëa's teasing arguments by speaking these words (Çrémad-
Bhägavatam 10.60.40):


jäòyaà vacas tava gadägraja. . .


   "My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, You drove off the
assembled kings with the resounding twang of Your Çärìga bow and then claimed me, Your fair
share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadägraja, for You to say You took shelter in the ocean
out of fear of those kings."***

   Lord Kåñëa's teasing words in the pastime were proper, for they were meant only to increase His
beloved's love for Him. Such words are approved by ancient and modern poets and philosophers.
Now jealous anger in the mood of worship, which is called {.sy 168}ädaraëéya-mäna", will be
considered. When, during the räsa dance, at the time of their first intimate meeting, Lord Kåñëa
abandoned all the gopés and remained hidden from their sight, the gopés became slightly angry with
Him. This is seen in the passage beginning with these words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.15):

sabhäjayitvä tam anaìga-dépanaà
   sahäsa-lélekñaëa-vibhrama-bhruvä
saàsparçanenäìka-kåtäìghri-hastayoù
   saàstutya iñat kupita babhasire


   "Sré Kåñëa had awakened romantic desires within the gopés, and they honored Him by glancing
at Him with playful smiles, gesturing amorously with their eyebrows, and massaging His hands and
feet as they held them in their laps. Even while worshiping Him, however, they felt somewhat
angry, and thus they addressed Him as follows."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadwva Gosvämé.

By speaking words of praise the lover may pacify the beloved's anger. An example of this may be
seen in these words of praise spoken by Lord Kåñëa to the gopés (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.32.21-22):


evaà mad-arthojjhita-loka-veda-
   svänäà hi vo mayy anuvåttaye 'baläù
mayäparokñaà bhajatä tirohitaà
   masuyitum marhatha tat priyam priyah


   "My dear girls, understanding that simply for My sake you had rejected the authority of worldly
opinion, of the Veòas and of your relatives, I acted as I did only to increase your attachment to Me.
Even when I removed Myself from your sight by suddenly disappearing, I never stopped loving you.
Therefore, My beloved gopés, please do not harbor any bad feelings toward Me, your beloved.***


na päraye 'haà niravadya-saàyujäm. . .


  "I am not able to repay My debt for your spotless service, even within a lifetime of Brahmä. Your
connection with Me is beyond reproach. You have worshiped Me, cutting off all domestic ties,
which are difficult to break. Therefore please let your own glorious deeds be your
compensation."***

  The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by the Supreme Personality of
Godhead.

Jealous anger or pride without a cause is called {.sy 168}praëaya-mäna" (anger or pride caused by
love). Such anger or pride has no external cause. Its only cause is the pastimes of love. The hero
(Lord Kåñëa) also manifests this kind of pride or anger. In the rasa of love for the Supreme
Personality of Godhead this kind of anger or pride is one of the uddépanas. An example of causeless
anger or pride, pride born of love, is seen in the passage that begins with these words of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.29.48):


täsäà tat-saubhaga-madaà
   vékñya mänaà ca keçavaù


   "Lord Keçava, seeing the gopés too proud of their good fortune, wanted to relieve them of this
pride and show them further mercy. Thus He immediately disappeared."***

  Here the gopés had pride born from love (pranaya-mana). There was a cause of their pride. They
were proud of their own good fortune. Therefore, to curb this pride and give them His mercy, Lord
Kåñëa suddenly disappeared from the gopés' sight. Then it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.36):


yäà gopém anayat kåñëo
  vihäyänyäù striyo vane. . .


   "The particular gopé whom Kåñëa had led to a secluded forest when He had abandoned all the
other girls began to think Herself the best of women. `My beloved has rejected all the other gopés',
She thought, `even though they are driven by Cupid himself. He has chosen to reciprocate with Me
alone.' "***

   Tbis gopé also became proud with love (praëaya-mäna). Filled with pride, She spoke these words
to Lord Kåñëa (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.37):


na päraye 'ham calituà
   naya mäà yatra te manaù


  "I cannot walk any further. Please carry Me wherever You want to go."***

   As the other gopés were previously, this gopé also became proud with love. Then, with anger also
born of love, Lord Kåñëa spoke to Her the following words (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.38):


skandha äruhyatäm. . .

   "Lord Kåñëa replied: `Just climb on My shoulder.' "***

   After speaking these words, Lord Kåñëa suddenly disappeared. The gopés have pride without
cause (ahetu) and Lord Kåñëa has pride with a faint reflection of a cause (hetv-äbhäsa). Flowing
through the great whirlpool of deceitful crookedness, the gopés' loving pride and anger become very
intense.When they are separated from Lord Kåñëa, their anger becomes sublimely pure. Lord
Kåñëa's other beloveds (other than the gopés) manifest grief, fear, and worry when they become
angry with a cause. As example of this is seen in the Çrémad-Bhägavatam chapter when Lord Kåñëa
teased Queen Rukmiëé with loving joking words. There Lord Kåñëa's intention was to make a
playful joke. Queen Rukmiëé was very deep and her love very sincere. There Lord Kåñëa thought:
"My wish is to enjoy pastimes of making My beloved angry. Her throat will be filled with emotional
words that reveal her great love for Me. However, she may not clearly understand My intention.
She will either become playfully angry, or she will say she does not undrstand My words. In this way
I will try to joke with her. Even when I made her brother very ugly-looking she still did not become
angry. It is not appropriate to continue in that direction. However, the happiness she feels by
associating with Me is the be-all-and-end-all of her life. It is everything for her. Perhaps by
mocking the pride she feels by being able to associate with Me I will make her angry. If she does not
become angry in that way, then perhaps by making her afraid that she will be separated from Me
she will speak many words revealing her love for Me." Thinking in this way, Lord Kåñëa spoke the
loving joking words that begin in this verse of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.10):


räja-putrépsitä bhüpaiù. . .


  "My dwear princess, you were sought after by many kings as powerful as the rulers of planets.
They were all abundantly endowed with polituical influence, wealth, beauty, generosity, and
physical strength."***

   That Lord Kåñëa was joking is also seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.9):


täà rüpiëém. . .prétaù smayan


  "As He contemplated her, the goddess of fortune herself, who desires only Him, Lord Kåñëa
smiled."***

   In this way it is seen that Lord Kåñëa was only joking. The sincerity of Queen Rukmiëé's love is
seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.25):


tad dåñövä bhagavän kåñëaù
   priyäyäù prema-bandhanam
häsya-prauòhim ajänantyäù

   karuëaù so 'nvakampata. . .


   "Seeing that His beloved was so bound to Him in love that she could not understand the full
meaning of His teasing, merciful Lord Kåñëa felt compassion for her.***
   "The Lord quickly got down from the bed. Manifesting four arms, He picked her up, gathered her
hair, and caressed her face with His lotus hand."***

   In these verses the word "häsya-prauòhim" means "the meaning of His joking words". Here Lord
Kåñëa proudly thought: "Even though she is very wise and profound, and even though her love is
very sincere, I will agitate her." The word "ajänantyäù" means "because there was no crookedness or
deceit in her sweet and sincere love, she did not understand the meaning of Lord Kåñëa's words".
This is described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.28):


häsya-prauòhi-bhramac-cittäm


   "Rukmiëé's mind was bewildered by Lord Kåñëa's clever joking."

  As a joke Lord Kåñëa had wished to see her playful anger. Thus He said to her in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.60.29-31):


mä mä vaidarbhy asüyetha
   jäne tväà mat-paräyaëäm
tvad-vacaù çrotu-kämena
   kñvelyäcaritam aìgane


   "O Vaidarbhé, do not be displeased with Me. I know that you are fully devoted to Me. I only
spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say.***


mukhaà ca prema-samrambha-
   sphuritädharam ékñitum
kaöä-kñepäruëäpäìgaà
   sundara-bhrü-kuöé-taöam


   "I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your
eyes throwing sidelong glances, and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown.***


ayaà hi paramo läbho
   gåheñu gåha-medhinäm

yan narmair iyate yämaù
   priyayä bhéru bhämini


   "The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is to spend time joking with their
beloved wives, My dear timid and tempermental one."***

   Although at first she was frightened, now Rukmiëé may be displeased. That is why Lord Kåñëa
now throws away the idea that Rukmiëé is meekly submissive to Him. Here the woprd {.sy
168}bhamini" is in the vocative case.

  Lord Kåñëa, who had yearned to see Rukmiëé reveal Her love for Him, says in Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.60.49):


sädhvy etac-chrotu-kämais tvaà
   räja-putri pralambhitä


   "O saintly lady, O princess, We deceived you only because We wanted to hear you speak like
this. Indeed, everything you said in reply to My words is most certainly true."***

   Wishing to refute Lord Kåñëa's assertyion of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.60.49 and also wishing to
reveal the truth about Lord Kåñëa, Queen Rukmiëé spoke these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.60.38):


tvaà vai samasta-puruñärtha-mayaù phalätmä. . .


   "You are the embodiment of all human goals and You are Yourself the final aim of life. Desiring
to attain You, O all-powerful Lord, intelligent persons abandon everything else. It is they who are
worthy of Your association, not men and women absorbed in the pleasure and grief resulting from
their mutual lust."***

  After understanding that Lord Kåñëa was only joking, Queen Rukmiëé manifested a little of the
anger that He had yearned to see. She said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.40):


jäòyaà vacas tava gadägraja. . .


   "My Lord, as a lion drives away lesser animals to claim his proper tribute, You drove off the
assembled kings with the resounding twang of Your Çärìga bow and then claimed me, Your fair
share. Thus it is sheer foolishness, my dear Gadägraja, for You to say You took shelter in the ocean
out of fear of those kings."***

   Here the word "jäòyam" means "great foolishness" just as "mädhuryam" means "great sweetness" in
these words of Çréla Bilvamaìgala Öhäkura's Çré Kåñëa-karëämåta (Text 68):


mädhuryam eva nu mano-nayanämåtaà nu


   "Lord Kåñëa is the great nectar sweetness that fills the eyes and the heart."

   In speaking these joking words, Lord Kåñëa's purpose was to agitate Queen Rukmiëé and destroy
the pride she felt in always having His association. This is seen in these words spoken by Çréla
Çukadeva Gosvämé in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.21):


etävad uktvä bhagavän
   ätmänaà vallabhäm iva
manyamänäm aviçleñät
   tad-darpa-ghna upäramat


   "Rukmiëé had thought herself especially beloved by the Lord because He never left her company.
By saying these things to her He vanquished her pride, and then He stopped speaking."***

   Lord Kåñëa had another purpose also, a purpose seen in these words He personally spoke in
Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.60.56):


bhrätur virüpa-karaëaà yudhi nirjitasya
  prodväha-parvaëi ca tad-vadham akña-goñöhyäm
duùkham samuttham asaho 'smad-ayoga-bhétyä
  naiväbravéù kim api tena vayaà jitäs te


   "When your brother, who had been defeated in battle and then disfigured, was later killed during
a gambling match on Aniruddha's wedding day, you felt unbearable grief, yet out of fear of losing
Me you spoke not a word. By this silence you have conquered Me."***

   In this chapter of Çrémad-Bhägavatam are seen Queen Rukmiëé's great love for Lord Kåñëa and
her natural absence of anger. From this it is seen that it certainly truthfully said that Lord Kåñëa's
beloveds love Him very dearly. When the manifestation of pride and anger is concluded, then
sambhoga is manifest. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.1):


itthaà bhagavato gopyaù
   çrutvä väcaù su-peçaläù

jahur viraha jaà täpam-
   tad-aìgopacitäçiñaù


   "When the cowherd girls heard the Supreme Personality of Godhead speak these most charming
words, they forgot their distress caused by separation from Him. Touching His transcendental
limbs, they felt all their desires fulfilled."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 387 and 388


   Now prema-vaicittyam will be considered. Its qualities are described in these words of Ujjvala-
nélamaëi, Çåìgära-bheda-prakaraëa (Text 134):


priyasya sannikarñe 'pi
   premotkarña-svabhävataù
yä viçleña-dhiyärtis tat
   prema-vaicittyam ucyate


   "When, even in the beloved's presence, the lover, out of intense love, is aggrieved with fears of
separation in the future, such a state is called prema-vaicittyam."

   Prema-vaicittyam is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.90.13-24):


kåñëasyaivaà viharato
   gaty-äläpekñita-smitaiù
narma-kñveli-pariñvangaiù
   stréëäà kila håtä dhiyaù


   "In this way Lord Kåñëa would sport with His queens, totally captivating their hearts with His
gestures, talks, glances, and smiles, and also with His jokes, playful exchanges, and embraces.***


ücur mukundaika-dhiyo
   girä unmatta-vaj jaòam
cintayantyo 'ravindäkñam
   täni me gadataù çåìu


   "The queens would become stunned in ecstatic trance, their minds absorbed in Kåñëa alone.

Then, thinking of their lotus-eyed Lord, they would speak as if insane. Please hear these words from
me as I relate them.***


çré-mahiñya ücuù

kurari vilapasi tvaà véta-nidrä na çeñe
   svapiti jagati rätryäm éçvaro gupta-bodhaù
vayam iva sakhi kaccid gäòha-nirviddha-cetä
   nalina-nayana-häsodära-lélekñitena


   "The queens said: O kurari bird, you are lamenting. Now it is night, and somewhere in this world
the Supreme Lord is asleep in a hidden place. But you are wide awake, O friend, unable to fall
asleep. Is it that, like us, you have had your heart pierced to the core by the lotus-eyed Lord's
munificent, playful smiling glances?"***


netre nimélayasi. . .


   "Poor cakraväké, even after closing your eyes, you continue to cry pitifully through the night for
your unseen mate. Or is it that, like us, you have become the servant of Acyuta and hanker to wear
in your braided hair the garland He has blessed with the touch of His feet?***


bho bhoù sadä niñöänase udanvann. . .


   "Dear ocean, you are always roaring, not sleeping at night. Are you suffering insomnia? Or is it
that, as with us, Mukunda has taken your insignias and you are hopeless of retrieving them?***


tvaà yakñmänä. . .


   "My dear moon, having contracted a severe case of tuberculosis, you have become so emaciated
that you fail to dispel the darkness with your rays. Or is it that you appear dumbstruck because, like
us, you cannot remember the encouraging promises Mukunda once made to you?***


kià nv äcäritam. . .


  "O Malayan breeze, what have we done to displease you, so that you stir up lust in our hearts,
which have already been shattered by Govinda's sidelong glances?***

megha çrémän. . .


   "O revered cloud, you are indeed dear ot the chief of the Yadus, who bears the mark of Çrévatsa.
Like us, you are bound to Him by love and are meditating upon Him. Your heart is distraught with
great eagerness, as our hearts are, and as you remember Him again and again you shed a torrent of
tears. Association with Kåñëa brings such misery!***


priya-räva. . .


   "O sweet-throated cuckoo, in a voice that could revive the dead you are vibrating the same
sounds we once heard from our beloved, the most pleasing of speakers. Please tell me what I can do
today to please you.***


na calasi. . .


   "O magnanimous mountain, you neither move nor speak. You must be pondering some matter of
great importance. Or do you, like us, desire to hold on your breasts the feet of Vasudeva's darling
son?***


çuñyad-dhradaù. . .


  "O rivers, wives of the ocean, your pools have now dried up. Alas, you have shriveled to nothing,
and your wealth of lotuses has vanished. Are you, then, like us, who are withering away because of
not receiving the affectionate glance of our dear husband, the Lord of Madhu, who has cheated our
hearts?***


haàsa svägatam äsyatäà piba payo brühy aìga çaureù kathäà
   dütaà tvaà nu vidäma kaccid ajitaù svasty asta uktaà purä
kià na vaç cala-sauhådaù smarati taà kasmäd bhajämo vayaà
   kñaudräläpaya käma-daà çréyam åte saivaika-niñöha striyam


   "Welcome, swan. Please sit here and drink some milk. Give us some news of the descendent of
Çüra, dear one. We know that you are His messenger. Is that invincible Lord doing well, and does
that unreliable friend of ours still remember the words He spoke to us long ago? Why should we go
and worship Him? O servant of a petty master, go tell Him who fulfills our desires to come here
without the goddess of fortune. Is she the only woman exclusively devoted to Him?"***

   Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.13 means: "With His gestures and other activities Lord captivated the
hearts of His queens as He enjoyed pastimes with them." Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.14 means: "Rapt
in meditation on Lord Kåñëa and thus momentarily speechless (agiraù), and again and again
maddened by their anuräga love, and meditating on playful lotus-eyed Kåñëa as if He were not
present before them, the gopés spoke words devoid of common sense. Please hear these words as I
relate them."
   Maddened by the touchof separation from Lord Kåñëa, the queens speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.90.15-24. Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.15 means: "O Kurari bird, all alone, you lament at night
somewhere in this world. Therefore you do not sleep. In some hidden place our master sleeps.
Thinking, "Because of the similar sweetness of your lament and our lament, we think. . . ", the
queens spoke the second half of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.15. In the following verses the queens
think similar ideas in otber ways. Then, thinking that, sent by the Lord, a swan has come as a
messenger before them, the queens speak Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.24. In that verse they say: {.sy
168}Does Kåñëa remember what He spoke to us in private? or does He not remember it?" In that
verse the word "ksaudra" means "O messenger of our fickle friend", {.sy 168}kämadam" means "who
agitates young girls", and {.sy 168}äläpaya" means "please call". Then the queens say: "We leave
everything for Him. He should comw without the goddess of fortune (sriyam rt). Here the queens
sarcastically pretend to glorify the goddess of fortune. They say: "Of all women the goddess of
fortune alone has true devotion to Lord Kåñëa. Therefore how is it possible that Lord Kåñëa will nto
be devoted to her." Speaking these words with voices choked with emotion, the queens sarcastically
speak of the goddess of fortune and also reveal their own love and devotion for Lord Kåñëa. That is
seen in this verse.
   After this manifestation of love-in-separation, the queens enjoy eternal sambhoga pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa. It is said of these queens (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.90.25):


itédåçena bhävena
    kåñëe yogeçvareçvare
kriyamänena mädhavyo
    lebhire paramäà gatim


  "By thus speaking and acting with such ecstatic love for Lord Kåñëa, the master of all masters of
mystic yoga, His loving wives attained the ultimate goal of life."***

  In this verse the words "gatià lebhire" mean {.sy 168}they attained an eternal relationship with

them, just as the elements ether, water, earth, air, and fire are the beginning and end of all material
objects and exist both within and without them."*
   "In this way all created beings reside within the basic elements of creation, while the spirit souls
pervade the creation, remaining in their own true identity. You should see both of these-the
material creation and the self-as manifest within Me, the imperishable Supreme Truth."***

   In the description of the Lord's Dämodara pastimes it is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.9.13-
14):


na cäntar na bahir yasya. . .


   "The Supreme Personality of Godhead has no beginning and no end, no exterior and no interior,
no front and no rear. In other words, He is all-pervading. Because He is not under the influence of
the element of time, for Him there is no difference between past, present and future. He exists in
His own transcendental form at all times. Being absolute, beyond relativity, He is free from

distinctions between cause and effect, although He is the cause and effect of everything. That
unmanifested person, who is beyond the perception of the senses, had now appeared as a human
child, and mother Yaçodä, considering Him her own ordinary child, bound Him to the wooden
mortar with a rope."*

   In these two verses are described some of Lord Kåñëa's eternal pastimes in Våndävana with the
people of Vraja, pastimes also revealed in the Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anucchedas 174-175. Those
pastimes are also considered here. The gopés were able to see Lord Kåñëa as the Supreme. That is
described in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.82.47):


adhyätma-çikñayä. . .


   "Having thus been instructed by Kåñëa in spiritual matters, the gopés were freed from all tinges
of false ego because of their incessant meditation upon Him. And with their deepening absorption
in Him, they came to understand Him fully."***
   In this verse the word "ätma" refers to Lord Kåñëa, and the word "siksaya" means "by His
instruction". Their bodies old and worn by meditating on Lord Kåñëa in the mood of separation, the
gopés then could see Lord Kåñëa in that way. Some thinkers interpret Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.82.45
in this way: "According to ordinary perception it seems that Lord Kåñëa is here preaching the
philosophy of Brahman, but that philosophy is not the true meaning of His words here. When
Rukmé was disfigured Lord Balaräma preached to Çré Rukmiëé what also seemed to be the
philosophy of Brahman. However, because Rukmiëé was directly enjoying pastimes with Lord
Kåñëa, that preaching of Lord Balarama's was only a specific pastime meant to look like the
activities of an ordinary person in this world. In the same way Lord Kåñëa's preaching of this
philosophy to the gopés is also only a pastime. Actually the gopés yearned to enjoy pastimes with
Lord Kåñëa directly in His spiritual form. This is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.82.48):


ähus ca te nalina-näbha padäravindaà


   "Dear Lord whose navel is just like a lotus flower, Your lotus feet are the only dhelter for those
who have fallen into the deep well of material existence. Your feet are worshiped and meditated
upon by great mystic yogis and highly learned philosophers. We wish that these lotus feet may also
be awakened within our hearts, although we are ordinary persons engaged in household affairs."***

   In this verse the gopés say: "Dear Lord whose navel is just like a lotus flower, may Your lotus feet
be awakened within the hearts of us, who are overcome by always meditating on You. Following
Your instructions, the peaceful-hearted kings of yoga meditate on Your feet in their hearts." An
explanation of this verse may be seen in the Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 170. This verse was
spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

In this way the truth of sambhoga, which consists of seeing, touching, and conversing with Lord
Kåñëa, is revealed. Lord Kåñëa stayed at Kurukñetra for three months. Then He and the gopés were
again separated. After that there were not again separatyion between them. After that they
enjoyed sambhoga pastimes together. The conclusion of these pastimes is described in the following
words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.83.1):


tathänugåhya bhagavän
   gopénäà sa gurur gatiù


   "Thus Lord Kåñëa, the spiritual master of the gopés and the very purpose of their life, showed
them His mercy. He •
then met with Yudhiñöhira and all His other relatives and inquired from them about their
welfare."***

   This verse explains that the gopés attained the desire they expressed in Çrémad-Bhägavatam
10.82.48. This is seen in this verse, which explains that Lord Kåñëa gave His mercy (anugåhya, to
them. This verse also affirms that they attained Lord Kåñëa, who is their eternal destination
(gatiù). This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

All of this is revealed in a passage from the Padma Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa, a passage quoted in
Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 176. In that pasasage it is said that Lord Kåñëa left Dvärakä and
returned to Våndävana. There, visible to everyone, even the ordinary people of this world, He
enjoyed pastimes for two months. After that Lord Kåñëa gave the people of Våndävana eternal
samyoga pastimes with Him, although those pastimes were not visible to ordinary people. Lord
Kåñëa clearly exlained all this to Uddhava in Çrémad-Bhägavatam's Eleventh Canto. There Lord
Kåñëa sais (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.10-11):


rämeëa särdhaà mathuräà praëéte. . .


   "The residents of Våndävana, headed by the gopés, were always completely attached to Me with
deepest love. Therefore, when My uncle Akrüra brought My brother Balaräma and Me to the city
of Mathurä, the residents of Våndävana suffered extreme mental distress because of separation from
Me and could not find any other source of happiness."***

täs täù kñapäù. . .


   "Dear Uddhava, all of those nights that the gopés spent with Me, their most dearly beloved, in
the land of Våndävana seemed to them to pass in less than a moment. Bereft of My association,
however, the gopés felt that those same nights dragged on forever, as if each night were equal to a
day of Brahmä."***

  After that time there was no further separation of Lord Kåñëa and the people of Våndävana.
After that time the people of Våndävana always enjoyed the bliss of Lord Kåñëa's association. Lord
Kåñëa described this truth in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (11.12.12-13):


tä nävidan mayy anuñaìga-baddha-dhiyaù. . .


   "My dear Uddhava, just as great sages in yoga trance merge into self realization like rivers
merging into the ocean, and are thus not aware of material names and forms, similarly the gopés
were so completely attached to Me within their minds that they could not think of their own
bodies, or of this world, or of their future lives. Their entire consciousness was simply bound up in
Me.***
   "All those hundreds of thousands of gopés, understanding Me to be their most charming lover
and ardently desiring Me in that way, were unaware of my actual position. Yet by intimately
associating with Me, the gopés attained Me, the Supreme Absolute Truth."***

    In these verses the word "anu" means "after the great separation", and "sanga-baddha-dhiyah"
means "their hearts were overcome with bliss", and navidan" means "they were bewildered with joy".
In that state it was as if they had become onbe with Lord Kåñëa. An example to explain that state is
given here in the phrase beginning with the words "just as great sages in yoga trance". A different
interpretation of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 11.12.13 has already been given in Kåñëa-sandarbha,
Anuccheda 177. What the gopés attained (präpuù, is described in this verse. It is briefly described
there. There it is said: "The gopés attained Me, the Supreme Brahman, who am named Kåñëa." Here
Lord Kåñëa hints: "Unaware of My true nature, that I am eternally the object of their love, the gopés
attained Me as their paramour (järam). Then, desiring Me as their husband, they eventually
attained Me as their husband (ramaëam)." In this way it is seen that the gopés' relationship with
Lord Kåñëa after some time becomes parakéyäbhäsa (the faint reflection of the love a girl has for
her paramour). All this is explained in that passage of Kåñëa-sandarbha, Anuccheda 177. My
glorious master, Çréla Rüpa Gosvämé explains in Ujjvala-nélamaëi (Näyikä-bheda-prakaraëa, Text
3):


neñöä yad aëgini rase kavibhiù paroòhä
   tad gokulämbuja-dåçäà kulam antareëa
äçaàsayä rasa-vidher avitäritänäà

  kaàsäriëä rasika-maëòala-çekhareëa


   "The lotus-eyed gopés of Gokula descended to this material world to enjoy amorous pastimes with
Kåñëa, the crest jewel of those expert at relishing transcendental mellows, and the enemy of King
Kaàsa. Except for those gopés, learned scholars and philosophers do not consider amorous affairs
between a married woman and a paramour to be good or auspicious."

   The scriptures explain that this was the activity at the time of Lord Kåñëa's descent to this
world. The conclusion of all this is found in Çréla Rüpa Gosvämé's Lalita-Mädhava (7.18), where it is
said:


dagdhaà hanta dadhänayä vapuù. . .


  "O moon-faced one, My dear friend ahs again come to Me. My desire to see Him scorched My
body and wounded My heart with a monsoohn of pain. My life-breeath yearns to meet Him in
Våndävana and enjoy pastimes with Him in a cottage by the Yamunä's shore."

    When the mistaken idea that He is their paramour is destroyed, then the gopés enjoy the full
bliss of perfect sambhoga pastimes with Lord Kåñëa. In this way vipralam,bha is divided into four
parts and sambhoga is also divided into four parts. In sambhoga are many different pastimes, such as
lélä-cauryam (playful theft), saëgänam (singing and music), räsa (the räsa dance), jala-kréòä (water
pastimes), and våndävana-vihära (pastimes in Våndävana forest). An example of playful theft is
seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.22.9):


täsäà väsäàsy upädäya
   népam äruhya satvaraù. . .


   "Taking the girls' garments, He quickly climbed to the top of a kaòamba tree. Then, as He
laughed loudly and His companions also laughed, He addressed the girls jokingly."***

  The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

An example of singing and music is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.9):


käcit samaà mukundena. . .

   "One gopé, joining Lord Mukunda in His singing, sang pure melodious tones that rose
harmoniously above His. Kåñëa was pleased and showed great appreciation for her performance,
saying `Excellent! Excellent!' Then another gopé repeated the same melody, but in a special metrical
pattern, and Kåñëa praised her also."***

   Another example of singing and music is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.34.20-
21):


kadäcid atha govindo
   rämaç cädbhuta-vikramaù
vijahratur vraje rätryäà
   madhya-gau vraja-yoñitäm


   "Once Lord Govinda and Lord Räma, the performers of wonderful feats, were playing in the
forest at night with the young girls of Vraja.***


upagéyamänau lalitaà
   stré janair baddha-sauhådaiù
sö-alaìkåtänuliptäìgau
   sragvinau virajo-'mbarau


   "Kåñëa and Balaräma wore flower garlands and spotless garments, and Their limbs were
beautifully decorated and anointed. The women sang Their glories in a charming way, bound to
Them by affection."***

   In general the Holi festival is celebrated in this way. Thus, to celebrate the Holi festival, Lord
Kåñëa and His brother, Lord Balaräma, enjoyed singing and many other pastimes with a host of girls
in Vraja. This pastime is also described in the Bhaviñya Puräëa, Uttara-khaëòa. Even today, the
people of India celebrate the Holi festival in this way. It is said in that passage of Çrémad-
Bhägavatam (10.34.22):


niçä-mukhaà mänayantäv
   uditoòupa-tärakam. . .


   "The two Lords praised the nightfall, signaled by the rising of the moon and the appearance of
stars, a lotus-scented breeze and bees intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine flowers."***

  The bliss of this festival, which occurs on the full-moon day of the month of Phälguna, after the
winter has ended, is described in this verse. Lord Kåñëa enjoyed this festival with His joyful friend
Lord Balaräma. In some texts of Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.34.20 the passage reads "vane rätryäm"

instead of "vraje rätryäm". In this reading the forest is described as the forest of Vraja. These verses
were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.


Anucchedas 425-427


   The räsa dance pastime is seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.2):


taträrabhata govindo
   räsa-kréòäm anuvrataiù. . .


   "There on the Yamunä's banks Lord Govinda then began the pastime of the räsa dance in the
company of those jewels among women, the faithful gopés, who joyfully linked their arms
together."***

   The Lord's water-pastimes are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.23):


so 'mbhasy alaà yuvatibhiù pariñicyamänaù. . .


   "My dear King, in the water Kåñëa found Himself being splashed on all sides by the laughing
gopés, who looked at Him with love. As the demigods worshiped Him by showering flowers from
their airplanes, the self-satisfied Lord took pleasure in playing like the king of the elephants."***

   Lord Kåñëa's pastimes in Våndävana forest are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.33.24):


tatas" ca kåñëopavane jala-sthala-
   prasüna-gandhänila juñöa-dik-tate. . .


   "Then the Lord strolled through a small forest on the bank of the Yamunä. This forest was filled
to its limits with breezes carrying the fragrances of all the flowers growing on the land and in the
water. Followed by His entourage of bees and beautiful women, Lord Kåñëa appeared like an
intoxicated elephant with his she-elephants."***

   The meaning of these verses is clear. These verses were spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

The Lord's amorous pastimes with the gopés are seen in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.29.46):


bähu-prasära-parirambha-karälakoru-névé. . .


   "There Kåñëa threw His arms around the gopés and embraced them. He aroused Cupid in the
beautiful young ladies of Vraja by touching their hands, hair, thighs, belts, and breasts, by playfully
scratching them with His fingernails, and also by joking with them, glancing at them, and laughing
with them. In this way the Lord enjoyed pastimes."***

   The meaning of this verse is clear. This verse was spoken by Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé.

At the conclusion of the descriptioon of Lord Kåñëa's amorous pastimes in the räsa dance it is
said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.33.25):


evaà çaçäìkäàçu-viräjitä niçäù. . .


   "Although the gopés were firmly attached to Lord Kåñëa, whose desires are always fulfilled, the
Lord was not internally affected by any mundane sex desire. Still, to perform His pastimes the Lord
took advantage of all those moonlit autumn nights, which inspire poetic descriptions of
transcendental affairs."***

   Lord Kåñëa's pastimes with Çré Rädhä, who is thhe crest jewel of all fortunate girls, are described
in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.27-34):


kasyäù padäni caitäni
   yätäyä nanda-sünunä
aàsa-nyasta-prakoñöhäyäù
   kareëoù kariëä yathä


   "Here we see the footprints of some gopé who must have been walking along with the son of
Nanda Mahäräja. He must have put His arm on Her shoulder, just as an elephant rests His trunk on
the shoulder of an accompanying she-elephant."***


anayärädhito nünaà
  bhagavän harir éçvaraù

yan no vihäya govindaù
   préto yäm amayad rahaù


   "Certainly this particular gopé has perfectly worshiped the allpowerful Personality of Godhead,
Govinda, since He was so pleased with Her that He abandoned the rest of us and brought Her to a
secluded place."***


dhanyä aho amé alyo
   govindäìghry-abja-reëavaù
yän brahmeçau ramä devé
   dadhur mürdhny agha-nuttaye


  "O girls! The dust of Govinda's lotus feet is so sacred that even Brahmä, Siva and the goddess
Ramä take that dust upon their heads to dispel sinful reactions."***


tasyä amüni naù kñobham-
   kurvanty uccaiù padäni yat
yaikäpahåtya gopénäà
   dhanaà bhuìkte 'cyutädharam

na lakñyante padäny atra
   tasyä nünaà tåëäìkuraiù
khidyat-sujätäìghri-talam
   unnénye preyaséà priyah


   "These footprints of that special gopé greatly disturb us. Of all the gopés, She alone was taken
away to a secluded place, where She is enjoying the lips of Kåñëa. Look, we can't see Her footprints
over here! It's obvious that the grass and sprouts were hurting the tender soles of Her feet, and so
the lover lifted up His beloved."***


imäny adhika-magnäni
   padäni vahato vadhüm
gopyaù paçyata kåñëasya
   bhäräkräntasya käminaù
aträvaropitä käntä
   puñpa-hetor mahätmanaù


   "Please observe, my dear gopés, how in this place lusty Kåñëa's footprints are pressed more deeply
into the ground. Carrying the weight of His beloved must have been difficult for Him. And over

here that intelligent boy must have put Her down to gather some flowers.***


atra prasünävacayaù
   pnya-rthe preyasä kåtaù
prapadäkramana ete
   paçyatäsakale pade


   "Just see how in this place dear Kåñëa collected flowers for His beloved. Here He has left the
impression of only the front part of His feet because He was standing on His toes to reach the
flowers."***


keça-prasädhanaà tö atra
   käminyäù käminä krtam
täni cüòayatä käntäm
   upaviñöam iha dhruvam


  "Certainly Kåñëa sat down here with His girlfriend to arrange Her hair. The lusty boy must have
made a crown for that Iusty girI out of the flowers He had collected."***

   In this passage Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.3027 is spoken by all the gopés, 10.30.28 is spoken by Çré
Rädhä's friends, 10.30.29 is spoken by the gopés who are neither friends nor enemies, 10.30.30 is
spoken by Çré Rädhä's rivals, the second stanza (beginning with the words "na lakñyate, of 10.30.30 is
spoken by Çré Rädhä's friends, who speak these words to torment Çré Rädhä's rivals, 10.30.31 is
spoken by the rivals who cannot bear Çré Rädhä's good fortune, the last two lines (beginning with
the word "aträvaropitä, of 10.30.31 and 10.30.32 are spoken by by Çré Rädhä's friends, the first two
lines of 10.30.33 are spoken by Çré Rädhä's rivals, and the last two lines of 10.30.33 are spoken by Çré
Rädhä's friends. In this way Çré Rädhä's friends and rivals describe the pastimes of Çré Çré Rädha'-
Kåñëa. It is also said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (10.30.26):


vilokyärtäù samabruvan


   "The gopés began following Kåñëa's path, as shown by His many footprints, but when they saw
that these prints were thoroughly intermixed with those of His dearmost consort, they became
perturbed and spoke as follows."***

  All the gopés spoke these words. Filled with lonmgings, all the gopés wandered (in the forest).
The passage quoted above (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 10.30.2*-34, was spoken by the vraja-gopés.

   The pastimes of Çré Rädha' had already been hinted at in these words of Çrémad-Bhägavatam
(10.30.11-12):

apy eëa-patni. . .


   "O friend, wife of the deer, has Lord Acyuta been here with His beloved, bringing great joy to
your eyes? Indeed, blowing this way is the fragrance of His garland of kunòa flowers, which was
smeared with the kuìkuma from the breasts of His girlfriend when He embraced Her.***
   "O trees, we see that you are bowing down. When the younger brother of Räma walked by here,
followed by the intoxicated bees swarming around the tulasé maïjarés decorating His garland, did
He acknowledge your obeisances with His affectionate glances? He must have been resting His arm
on the shoulder of His beloved and carrying a lotus flower in His free hand."***

   The reader may study these verses to see the pastimes of Çré Çré Rädhä-Kåñëa.


Epilogue


   Many verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam's Tneth Canto we have not elaborately explained here. The
devotees who yearn to taste the nectar of the rasas may study the explanations Çréla Çrédhara Svämé
has given in His Daçama-öippané commentary. Following his explanations, we have explained the
verses of Çrémad-Bhägavatam.


älébhiù paripälitaù pravalitaù sänandam älokitaù
   pratyäçaà sumanaù-phalodaya-vidhau sämodam äsväditaù
våndäraëya-bhuvi prakäça-madhuraù sarvätiçäyi-çriyä
   rädhä-mädhavayoù pramodayatu mäm ulläsa-kalpa-drumaù


   May the glorious kalpa-våkña tree of Çré Çré Rädha'-Mädhava, a tree surrounded by hosts of
bumblebees that are Çré Rädhä's gopé freinds, a tree delightful to see, a tree that fills the directions
with the sweet fragrance of its sumanù flowers, a tree that manifests in the land of Våndävana the
sweetness of the greatest beauty and handsomeness, fill me with delight.


tädåça-bhävaà bhävaà
   prathayitum iha yo 'vatäram äyätaù
ä-durjana-gaëa-çaraëaà
   sa jayati caitanya-vigrahaù kåñëaù


   Glory to Lord Kåñëa, who is the shelter of everyone, including even the most fallen and wicked,
and who, manifesting the form of Lord Caitanya, descended to this world to widely distribute the
gift of ecstatic spiritual love.

Thus ends Çré Préti-sandarbha

tasyäravinda-nayanasya. . .

jijïäsitam adhétaà ca. . .


   "You have fully delineated the subject of impersonal Brahman as well as the knowledge derived

  The superiority of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is also confirmed by these words of
Dhruva Mahäräja (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 4.9.10):


yä niåvrtis tanu-bhåtäm. . .


   "My Lord, the transcendental bliss derived from meditating upon Your lotus feet or hearing
about Your glories from pure devotees is so unlimited that it is far beyond the stage of
brahmänanda, where one thinks himself merged in the impersonal Brahman as one with the
Supreme. Since brahmänanda is also defeated by the transcendental bliss derived from devotional
service, then what to speak of the temporary blissfulness of elevating oneself to the heavenly
planets, which is ended by the separating sword of time? Although one may be elevated to the
heavenly planets, he falls down in due course of time."*

   About the author of Çrémad-Bhägavatam it is said (Çrémad-Bhägavatam 12.12.69):


svasukha-nibhåta-cetäs tad-vyudastänya-bhävaù. . .


    "I offer my respectful obeisances unto Çréla Çukadeva Gosvämé, the son of Vyäsadeva. He is the
destroyer of all sinful reactions and is full in self-realization and bliss. Because of this, he has no
other desire. Still, he was attracted by the transcendental pastimes of the Supreme Personality of
Godhead, and out of compassion for the people, he described the transcendental historical
literature called Çrémad-Bhägavatam. This is compared to the light of the Absolute Truth."*

   In Bhagavad-gétä (18.54) the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself declares:


brahma-bhütaù prasannätmä. . .


   "One who is thus transcendentally situated at once realizes the Supreme Brahman. He never
laments nor desires to have anything. He is equally disposed to every living entity. In that state he
attains pure devotional service unto Me."*

    Simply by seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Çré Prahläda became free from all sins.
Fiorst he saw the impersonal Brahman, then he saw the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and then
he became filled with transcendental bliss. In this way he attained the supreme goal of life. Of him
it is said in Çrémad-Bhägavatam (7.9.6):


sa tat-kara-sparça-dhutäkhiläçubhaù
   sapady abhivyakta-parätma-darçanaù
tat-päda-padmaà hådi nirvåto dadhau
